messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert triggered — prometheus.scrape.failures x3 for job=metrics-pipeline, source=prometheus-exporter-cluster. Severity: page.

pagerduty: Page fired to oncall (maria). Incident key: pd_1864123456_metrics_scrape.

maria (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it. Quick context: dashboards showing drop in kube_pod_container_status_ready and some missing node metrics.

ryan: I see logs-ingest consumer lag rising in Kafka, offsets behind ~120k. Could be related if exporters are overwhelmed and pushing back.

olivia: grafana panels time out when fetching node/cadvisor series. Prometheus logs show scrape_timeout and EOF on some exporter endpoints.

maria (oncall): attaching recent prometheus-exporter log snippet:```
2026-02-12T14:20:33Z exporter-1 ERROR http: read tcp 10.0.2.45:49382->10.0.3.12:9100: i/o timeout
2026-02-12T14:20:37Z exporter-1 WARN scrape failed for target node-exporter-10-0-3-12:9100: connection refused
2026-02-12T14:21:01Z prometheus ERROR scrape_manager: scrape failed, target=https://exporter.svc.cluster.local:9100, err="context deadline exceeded"
```

tom: @maria can you confirm if this is only a subset of exporters or the whole cluster? If it's cluster-wide, maybe prometheus scrape throughput. If subset, could be network issues or a noisy node.

maria (oncall): initial grep shows ~18% of exporter pods returning errors, scattered across two AZs (az-2 and az-3). Not just one host.

ryan: Kafka backlog + partial exporter failures -> ingestion sidecar retries may be spiking. @ingest-bot can you surface consumer group lag and pod CPU for ingest consumers?

ingest-bot: consumer_group=metrics-ingest-cg lag=127436, consumers=6, average_lag_per_consumer=21239; ingest-consumer pods CPU 95% on 3 pods, others 30%.

olivia: CPU spike on 3 consumers suggests hot-sharding. Could be that Prometheus is retrying many targets and producing bursts.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan (quick):
1) Temporarily increase prometheus scrape_timeout from 10s -> 15s for job=metrics-pipeline to reduce failed scrapes noise.
2) Scale prometheus-exporter Deployment from 3 -> 6 replicas (kubectl scale deploy exporter --replicas=6).
3) Throttle high-cardinality metric groups by applying a relabel_config drop for kube_pod_labels and long label sets for 30m.
4) Scale metrics-ingest consumers from 6 -> 9 to catch up lag.

olivia: agree. Add step 0: create short-lived alert suppression in Grafana for the noisy panels so oncall isn't flooded while we fix.

maria (oncall): performing step 2 now:```
kubectl -n monitoring scale deploy prometheus-exporter --replicas=6 && kubectl rollout status deploy/prometheus-exporter -n monitoring --timeout=2m
```

maria (oncall): step 1 applied via configmap edit and restart of prometheus config reload:```
# prometheus scrape config snippet
- job_name: 'metrics-pipeline'
  scrape_interval: 15s
  scrape_timeout: 15s
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['exporter.svc.cluster.local:9100']
```

tom: while that's happening I'll run tcpdump on a couple of exporter nodes to see if network timeouts align with pod CPU/network saturation.

ryan: scaling ingest consumers now:```
kubectl -n analytics scale deploy metrics-ingest-consumers --replicas=9
```

ingest-bot: scale request accepted. New pods pending, will rebalance partitions.

maria (oncall): after scaling exporters and ingest consumers: monitoring shows exporter error rate dropping ~60% in last 120s, consumer lag trending down to 42k. Dashboard panels starting to return.

olivia: good. Any indication of root cause? Could be networking hiccup in AZs or a Prometheus overload due to a large scrape churn.

maria (oncall): preliminary root cause hypothesis: bursty scrape retries from Prometheus combined with a small set of CPU-starved exporter pods (OOM kill earlier this morning) created cascading retries and Kafka backlog. We had a recent config change that added more scrape targets for a new feature — might have increased cardinality.

tom: suggest follow-ups:
- check recent deploys for exporter and any autoscaler events (kube events)
- add vertical/auto-scaling to exporter or increase resource requests
- revert new high-cardinality metrics until we size properly

ryan: notifying product analytics teams about potential missing historical metrics for ~15min window (14:18-14:34 UTC).

maria (oncall): notifying via #product-analytics: "Heads up — transient metrics gaps observed ~14:18-14:34 UTC. We're mitigating and will follow up."

olivia: prepping post-incident action items: one: add circuit-breaker in Prometheus relabel rules to drop particularly expensive targets after X failures, two: add per-target scrape jitter to smooth bursts, three: add alert for consumer CPU > 80% for 2m.

maria (oncall): current status: customer-facing dashboards degraded but recovering; alert flood suppressed; ingestion lag decreasing. I'm going to hand this to @olivia for overnight watch and run a deeper postmortem tomorrow.

olivia: taking over. I'll keep an eye for 2 hours, collect logs, and draft RCA template. Assigning follow-ups: @tom investigate network at AZ boundary, @ryan validate config change that added targets, @maria schedule postmortem.

pagerduty: Incident pd_1864123456 acknowledged by maria. Escalation stopped.

incident-bot: Incident closed for paging purposes — monitoring continues.

maria (oncall): thanks team. leaving notes in incident tracker: "temporary scrape timeout increase and exporter scaling applied. Follow-ups required: resource tuning and card reduction. No ongoing customer errors, dashboards recovering."

olivia: ETA for follow-ups doc 24h. Handoff complete. :handshake:
